mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that support corporate earnings growth and investor confidence, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 2.0%, it signals active monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates and compresses valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates synchronized labor and goods market expansion that boosts corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS and INDPRO both rising) fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime with housing starts (HOUST) above 1000 thousand units and CPIAUCSL rising above 2.5% year-over-year, inflationary pressures and potential Fed tightening cause negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST exceeds 1000 and CPIAUCSL rises above 2.5% YoY, SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the regime-specific Rank IC is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) reflects strong consumer demand and economic momentum that supports corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when HOUST increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 900 thousand units, it signals weakening consumer demand and economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (HOUST < 900.0), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply contraction regime marked by declining industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 and rising unemployment (UNRATE) above 5.0%, economic slowdown and reduced corporate profitability drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO falls below 100 and UNRATE rises above 5.0%, SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the regime-specific Rank IC is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates active monetary tightening that compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS both rising) fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
